description: Swedish Act (2017:630) on Measures against Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing. Transposes EU AMLD4 into Swedish law. Chapter structure: Ch.1 Definitions, Ch.2 CDD, Ch.3 Ongoing Monitoring, Ch.4 SAR Reporting, Ch.5 Specialist Services, Ch.6 Internal Controls, Ch.7 Registration, Ch.8 Supervision, Ch.9 Penalties.

canonical_name: Finnish Act on Preventing Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (444/2017)
description: Finnish Act 444/2017 (Rahanpesun ja terrorismin rahoittamisen estäminen) transposing AMLD4. Administered by Finanssivalvonta (FIN-FSA). Covers CDD, ongoing monitoring, suspicious transaction reporting, internal controls, and registration of obliged entities.

Norwegian Money Laundering Act of 1 June 2018. Transposes AMLD4. Administered by Finanstilsynet. EEA agreement means Norway implements EU AML directives with some delay. Key provisions: CDD, beneficial ownership, SAR to Økokrim, internal controls.

canonical_name: Danish Hvidvaskloven (Act on Measures to Prevent Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism)
description: Danish consolidated Money Laundering Act transposing EU AML directives. Most recent consolidation: Act No. 1134 of 2019 as amended. Administered by Finanstilsynet and Erhvervsstyrelsen.

canonical_name: SE Penningtvättslagen Ch. 2 — Customer Due Diligence
description: Chapter 2 of Swedish Penningtvättslagen covering CDD obligations: customer identification and verification, beneficial ownership, purpose of business relationship, ongoing monitoring. Risk-based approach determines depth of CDD measures.
Chapter 3 of Swedish Penningtvättslagen covering ongoing monitoring obligations: transaction scrutiny, customer profile updates, monitoring of complex and unusual transactions.

Chapter 4 of Swedish Penningtvättslagen covering the obligation to report suspicions of money laundering or terrorist financing to Finanspolisen. Tipping-off prohibition. Attorney-client privilege exception for lawyers.

Chapter 6 of Swedish Penningtvättslagen covering internal controls: written AML/CFT policies and procedures, central function (MLRO), employee training, independent audit function, group-level obligations.

canonical_name: FI ML Act Ch. 3 — Customer Due Diligence
description: Chapter 3 of Finnish ML Act 444/2017 covering CDD: customer identification and verification, risk classification, beneficial ownership, purpose of relationship, simplified and enhanced due diligence.

canonical_name: FI ML Act Ch. 4 — Suspicious Transaction Reporting
description: Chapter 4 of Finnish ML Act covering the obligation to report suspicions to the Finnish Financial Intelligence Unit (FIVA-FIU / Rahanpesun selvittelykeskus) within the National Bureau of Investigation (KRP).

canonical_name: NO Hvitvaskingsloven Ch. 2 — Customer Due Diligence
description: Chapter 2 of Norwegian Hvitvaskingsloven covering CDD: customer identification, verification, beneficial ownership (reelle rettighetshavere), business relationship purpose, ongoing monitoring.

canonical_name: NO Hvitvaskingsloven — SAR Reporting to Økokrim
description: Norwegian Hvitvaskingsloven requirement to report suspicions (MT-rapportering) to Finanskriminalitetsenheten (Økokrim), the Norwegian Economic Crime Unit which serves as FIU.
Danish Hvidvaskloven CDD provisions covering customer identification, beneficial ownership (reelle ejere), business relationship purpose, simplified and enhanced due diligence, ongoing monitoring.

canonical_name: DK Hvidvaskloven — SAR Reporting to Hvidvasksekretariatet
description: Danish Hvidvaskloven requirement to report suspicious transactions (underretning) to Hvidvasksekretariatet, the Danish FIU operating under the State Prosecutor for Serious Economic and International Crime (SØIK).

Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (FI). Primary AML/CFT supervisor for credit institutions, investment firms, insurance, and payment services in Sweden. Issues supervisory guidance and conducts AML inspections.

Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority. AML/CFT supervisor for credit institutions, investment firms, and payment services in Finland. Publishes thematic reviews and issues supervisory guidelines on AML.
Norwegian Financial Supervisory Authority. AML/CFT supervisor for Norwegian financial institutions and registered obliged entities. Issues thematic supervisory letters and AML inspection reports.
Danish Financial Supervisory Authority. AML/CFT supervisor for Danish financial sector. Works alongside Erhvervsstyrelsen for DNFBP supervision. Issues risk assessments and supervisory guidelines.

Swedish Financial Intelligence Unit, operating as a unit within the Swedish Police Authority (Polismyndigheten). Receives and analyses SARs (misstankerapporter) from obliged entities. Part of FIU.net.

Finnish Financial Intelligence Unit, operating within the National Bureau of Investigation (Keskusrikospoliisi / KRP). Receives and processes STRs (rahanpesuilmoitukset) from Finnish obliged entities.

Norwegian Economic Crime Unit serving as the national FIU. Receives MT-rapporter from Norwegian obliged entities. Also prosecutes economic crime including money laundering. Part of Norwegian Police Service.

Danish Financial Intelligence Unit, operating under the State Prosecutor for Serious Economic and International Crime (SØIK). Receives underretninger (suspicious transaction reports) from Danish obliged entities.

Swedish term for obliged entities (verksamhetsutövare) under the Penningtvättslagen. Includes financial institutions, lawyers, accountants, real estate agents, company formation agents, and crypto service providers.

Swedish term for beneficial owner (verklig huvudman). The natural person(s) who ultimately own or control a legal entity. Registered in the Swedish Bolagsverket beneficial ownership register under the Lag om registrering av verkliga huvudmän (2017:631).
Swedish term for suspicious activity report (misstankerapport). Must be filed with Finanspolisen when ML/TF suspicion arises. Tipping-off (varning) is prohibited under Ch. 4 Penningtvättslagen.

Swedish term for the business-wide risk assessment (verksamhetsriskbedömning) required under Penningtvättslagen Ch. 2 §1. Must be documented and updated regularly. Basis for calibrating CDD intensity.

Finnish statutory definition of money laundering (rahanpesu) under the Criminal Code (Rikoslaki). Corresponds to AMLD and FATF definitions. Includes conversion, transfer, concealment, acquisition, and use of proceeds of crime.

Norwegian term for money laundering (hvitvasking). Defined in the Norwegian Penal Code (Straffeloven § 332-333). The Hvitvaskingsloven provides the preventive framework; prosecution occurs under Straffeloven.
Danish term for money laundering (hvidvask). Defined in Danish Criminal Code and operationalised by Hvidvaskloven. Danish FIU data shows real estate and crypto sectors as high-risk sectors.

All Nordic countries maintain public or semi-public beneficial ownership registers: Swedish Bolagsverket (verkliga huvudmän), Finnish PRH (todelliset edunsaajat), Norwegian Brønnøysund (reelle rettighetshavere), and Danish Erhvervsstyrelsen (reelle ejere). Part of AMLD5 transposition.

All four Nordic countries publish national risk assessments of ML/TF risks. Sweden: Nationell riskbedömning (FI+Finanspolisen). Finland: National risk assessment (Ministry of Finance). Norway: Nasjonal risikovurdering. Denmark: National risk assessment.

Swedish Penningtvättslagen (2017:630) will be substantially superseded by AMLR 2024/1624 from 10 July 2027. Customer-facing AML obligations (CDD, monitoring, SAR, internal controls) will be governed directly by AMLR. AMLD6 transposition required by 10 July 2026.
Finnish ML Act 444/2017 will be substantially superseded by AMLR 2024/1624 from 10 July 2027. Finland must transpose AMLD6 by 10 July 2026, implementing institutional and criminal sanctions changes.

Norway implements EU AML directives via the EEA Agreement with some delay. AMLD4 was incorporated (2019). AMLD5 incorporated later. AMLR will need EEA Joint Committee decision before being incorporated. Timeline differs from EU member states.

canonical_name: FATF Mutual Evaluation Reviews — Nordic Countries
description: All Nordic countries have undergone FATF mutual evaluation reviews. Key results: Norway (2014, high maturity), Denmark (2017, effective implementation), Finland (2019, strong framework), Sweden (2023/2024 evaluation cycle). Reviews assess effectiveness against FATF Recommendations.

All Nordic AML laws prohibit tipping off — informing a customer or third party that a SAR has been or may be filed. Swedish: varningsförbudet. Finnish: ilmoituskielto. Norwegian: informasjonsforbud. Danish: underretningsforbud.

Swedish term for the AML/CFT central function (penningtvättsansvarig) required under Penningtvättslagen Ch. 6. Must be a senior person with appropriate authority, resources, and access. Responsible for managing internal controls, staff training, and SAR filings.

Nordic AML laws require EDD for PEPs, high-risk third countries, and complex/unusual transactions. Sweden: utökad kundkännedom. Finland: tehostettu tuntemisvelvollisuus. Norway: forsterkede kundetiltak. Denmark: skærpet kundekendskab.

PEP definitions under Nordic AML laws broadly follow AMLD4 standards. Nordic countries have domestic PEP lists including heads of state, senior politicians, judges, central bank governors, and senior military. Former PEPs require risk-based continued monitoring.

Finansinspektionen's AML/CFT supervisory inspection process: off-site document reviews, on-site inspections, themed inspections (e.g., crypto, real estate), and follow-up enforcement actions. Published inspection findings contribute to sector-wide guidance.

Process for filing suspicious activity reports across the Nordic countries: Sweden uses goAML system via Finanspolisen; Finland reports to Rahanpesun selvittelykeskus; Norway uses the EFIN system at Finanskriminalitetsenheten; Denmark reports to Hvidvasksekretariatet.

Under AMLA Regulation 2024/1620, AMLA will coordinate supervisory colleges for cross-border institutions with significant Nordic presence. Nordic supervisors (FI, FIN-FSA, Finanstilsynet NO/DK) participate. Convergence with AMLA methodology required.
